about: THE MARKET's level: where every place is. Map tiles, x east, y north; the block runs from front y -77 back to -92.4. The builders read this file; the map editor exports it. A place's face (n, e, s or w; n if none) is the side its front looks out of, onto its street.

sections.note: the eight sections round Central Park, 4 across and 2 up, each A's size; ids[col][row]; ring: the park inside the ring street, the street's outer edge, its sidewalks' width, the depth of the row of buildings on its outer side, then the water and its shore walk past the top and bottom rows

places.note: the skate park (src/111fd-skatepark.js), out in the open in this section's park: its middle, the way its gate faces, its size in x and y (map units)
the skate pit (src/111fda-skatepit.js), a large concrete bowl out in the open deeper in this section's park: its middle and its size in x and y (map units); sunk: the far ground is cut over it

sides.note: sidewalk widths, outer then park side: ns the south and north streets (Market St), we the west and east (West St)

loop.note: THE LOOP: the subway under the ring streets. tracks are the rails' lines (map tiles) round the ring, r the corners' radius; trains run the timetable from the clock, stopping dwell seconds at every station; speed tiles/s, accel tiles/s/s

west.note: no road (owner, 10 Nov 2026: "No roads in park at all"): the park runs to the section's west edge; x0/x1 stay as the measures the street's layout is drawn from

places.name: SUBWAY STAIRS
places.note: on Market St between the arcade and the theatre, over the loop's straight (owner, 10 Nov 2026: back from the Hudson promenade)

places.name: THE FISH MARKET
places.note: the Hudson row east of the way through (owner, 9 Nov 2026): the yard, the tin shed, the brick shed (x spans), the highway over the promenade (y span, deck height in metres, a bent every so many tiles); stalls: a wholesaler each (who: its record in characters.json)

guitar.note: the park's guitar on its stand, anyone's to play (146zob-guitar): park tiles, hd the way it faces in degrees

bigLake.note: THE BIG LAKE (owner, 7 Nov 2026): centred on the park's north-east corner, rx by ry map tiles; a quarter in Section A, the rest past the forcefield, seen, never walked; the brook runs out of it to THE LAKE (the pond)

tower4.watch: the dungeon stair (owner, 10 Nov 2026: towers near anything that has monsters or danger in the park)

tower5.watch: the big lake's west shore and its ice

tower6.watch: the ghosts' island and its footbridge

brook.note: the brook's course from its spring to the lake (map tiles); the lake's middle ends it

digs.note: THE FOSSIL DIGS (owner, 10 Nov 2026: "fossil digs"): where fossils lie in the park (src/150cyc-fossils.js), map tiles; size the radius its holes are dug in, holes how many (each dug once a day), finds the animals by RARITY tier (c, r, s), band the diggers its sign asks for, deco the Polyfork bones lying there

sites.note: the bath house on its island in the lake: no trees or paths here
where the island's footbridge lands: no trees here
the public observatory (owner, 10 Nov 2026): the dome and the lawn round it; no trees or paths here
the park orchard (owner, 10 Nov 2026): eight plots, one a player, for the fruit trees (src/147d); no trees or paths here

parkPlaces.stallsNote: the park wall's stalls (owner, 8 Nov 2026): side w or e of the park gate, slot 0 nearest it; merchant the character who keeps it, goods what its table shows (STALL.GOODS)

islands.note: the bath house's island in the middle of the lake (owner, 8 Nov 2026): ghosts float out to it

bridges.note: the bath house island's footbridge to the shore, walked off once you are alive again (owner, 8 Nov 2026)

falls.note: THE FALLS (owner, 10 Nov 2026): Central Park's waterfall beside the big lake, between the brook and the giant tree; map tiles: x, y the plunge pool's middle, r its radius, box the rock massif, lobe the pool's south lobe under big tree A's rope swing; h the cliff's height in metres

racks.note: the brochure racks on the street (159k-brochures): map tiles, rot the way one faces in radians

editor.note: the editor's own extras (added things, trees, looks); the game does not read these yet

bigTrees.note: THE BIG TREES (owner, 7 Nov 2026; redone 10 Nov 2026): map tiles; kind A level branch, B rising, C low and sagging, G the giant (a hollow shell of leaves round thick limbs to climb); face: where the big branch reaches, degrees; climb: SPACE next to it climbs it; s: its size, 1 a 62 m tree (owner, 10 Nov 2026: "move back towards park area and make them 25-50% smaller, and add 20 more scattered around. i want 1 giant big tree ... its 2x bigger")

edge.note: THE NEW MAP'S EDGES (owner, 6 Nov 2026): lines in map tiles you cannot cross (a forcefield where you press on one); past them only the backdrop, seen, never walked
edge.carryNote: the park carried on past the north and east edges (owner, 10 Nov 2026: "the cut off for rest of the park should seem seamless"; of the options: "Carry the real park on"): this many tiles of its own grass, the big lake's shore, track, rocks and trees, then the far picture

ground.note: the land past the edges (owner, 7 Nov 2026: "set a base color for far off distance things like grass"; 8 Nov 2026: the whole of Central Park, the city round it): one low-res picture under everything outside the section: grass in park (the far park's box, twice the ring's park each way, owner 10 Nov 2026), outer (its streets' outer edge) road, the city past them in blocks (city, its streets every block tiles); the park's waters and lawns (x, y, rx, ry, turn in degrees) and paths ([x,y] points, the drive and the cross roads); the big lake's whole shore in it (box x0, y0, x1, y1 in tiles; tiles a pixel; colours)

strips.note: the streets carried on past the edges, low-res ground (x0, y0, x1, y1, kind)

park.note: Central Park past the forcefield, the whole of it (owner, 8 Nov 2026: Manhattan): plain low trees in bands (x0, y0, x1, y1 in tiles) inside edge.ground.park (n of them, and clumps: bunches of bigger trees), none in the clearings (x, y, rx, ry: the reservoir, the lawns, the ponds) or on the paths (edge.ground.paths)

city.note: the far city (owner, 8 Nov 2026: Manhattan, the whole island; only the outline past what the view reaches, no shapes): a painted ring all round. In tiles: center, water (the Hudson, a y band), lowY/lowK (past this y the far shore, lower), east (the East River: its near bank as [x,y] points along the island, its width; past the island's ends all water; across it the far shore, lowK), base (lowest, highest), clusters (x, y, peak, radius: downtown, midtown, uptown, the far shore's), ring (the outline's layers, the first just past the view; a direction that meets the Hudson at the last one is water all the way), panorama (the ring's radius)

blocks.note: the city's buildings past the park (owner, 10 Nov 2026: "fill it out logical with the rest of the buildings in NYC"): plain boxes on every block of edge.ground's city within depth tiles of the park's streets, one draw; lots across a block (two rows, each lot min to max tiles wide), a storey's height (px, as the rows'), storeys low then tall on a block's ends (avenue), the row facing the park (park: how often, storeys), towers further out (how often near and far, storeys, how much taller far); past them the painted skyline

far.note: the water past the river: shore, where it ends (the far bank, a map y); ends: how far the far water and its shore run (map x); list: rows of shapes on the far shore, none (owner, 8 Nov 2026: only the outline past the view)

mirror.note: Market St past its ends (owner, 8 Nov 2026: "lets make the street look the same all the way down"): the street's band (y0, y1 in tiles) drawn again mirrored at the forcefields (x: west, east), reach tiles out, from these builders' groups; each side drawn while you are within show tiles of it; the lawn and the far grass leave the street's ground (y0, y1) to it
